clue.text: Bill Dad's accepted at centre of Faro inn?

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar
Pa is an informal name for Dad, with the 's kept

indicators.note: only the core of the place name is wanted, its two middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of the Portuguese town's name

explanation.surface: A father picks up the bill at an inn in the middle of Faro, on the Algarve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Portuguese setting of Faro is a fair hint at an Iberian eating place; the question mark admits that an inn is only loosely the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapas bar is a Spanish-style drinking establishment serving small dishes, here loosely called an inn by example.

clue.text: Monarch ignored by PM once in part of House?

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so these letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, a former British Prime Minister
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: The Queen pointedly snubbed by a former Prime Minister somewhere in the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H on House suggests Parliament, fitting the PM; it is just any house, whose roof may be of thatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed roofing material, so it forms one part of a cottage or other dwelling.

clue.text: Supporter of natural lipstick upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
the answer is formed out of the run of letters across the next words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A fan of natural lipstick is upset about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column that holds up a structure, so it is a supporter in the literal, architectural sense.

clue.text: Alone in fix, am set to change — this might help?

indicators.note: the letters are set to change, that is to be rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone alone in a tight spot is determined to change, and wonders what would help.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells a story: someone stuck alone and wanting to change would be helped by looking hard at themselves, which the definition leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-examination, honest scrutiny of one's own conduct, is what might help a person who is resolved to change.

clue.text: Saying used in publicity pages extremely deficient

indicators.note: deficient at the extremes means lacking its two end letters

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slogan that appears in very poor advertising pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb or traditional saying, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Took care of Independent at sea?

indicators.note: at sea read as in the sea, so the abbreviation sits inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
IND is a standard abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: Asks whether an independent sailor looked after things while out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Independent nods to the newspaper running the puzzle; it is just the abbreviation tucked into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind something is to look after it, so minded is a past-tense synonym of took care of.

clue.text: Old ruler in river battle he contrived

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially put together, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler contrived a battle on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, known as Ivan the Terrible, was the sixteenth-century tsar of Russia, a historical sovereign.

clue.text: Park area?

parts.note: surface reading: a part of a public park, with lawns and paths
setter's reading: park is the verb, a place where you leave the car at home

explanation.walkthrough: Park reads as a noun for green space, but it is the verb: the answer is the private strip where a car is parked.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private road beside a house where a car is usually left, an area for parking.

clue.text: Going down to see protest over money (not one to participate)

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the protest comes first

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a public protest

indicators.note: a thing that participates gets inside the action, so the letter goes within the money word

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
not one is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone goes along to watch a protest about pay, but won't join in.
explanation.walkthrough: Not one means nought, the letter O, which participates by entering the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotion is being moved down in rank, so it is a going down in status.

clue.text: Permission to proceed unlike 21?

parts.note: the go-ahead signal
21 across is an area of uncertainty; its opposite is everything being perfectly plain

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the answer at 21 across, places where nothing is definite; read literally, the answer is their opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The all clear is a signal that danger has passed and it is safe to go on, permission to proceed.

clue.text: Marxist activists operating in Sinic manner first of all?

definitions.text: Marxist activists operating in Sinic manner first of all?

indicators.note: the first letter of every word in the run is what is taken

parts.words: Marxist activists operating in Sinic manner
parts.note: the opening letters of the six words

explanation.surface: Describes Marxist activists working in the Chinese way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinic means Chinese; the whole clue both builds the answer and describes it, as Chinese-style Marxism.
explanation.definitionFit: Maoism is the Chinese form of Marxism developed by Mao Zedong, followed by activists working in that manner.

clue.text: Part of diocese being standard? Sort of

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
the suffix meaning sort of, as in reddish

explanation.surface: Asks whether a part of a diocese is pretty much normal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is divided into parishes, each with its own church and priest, so a parish is a subdivision of it.

clue.text: Stretch to see wading bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... one's neck, to stretch it to get a view
second meaning: a tall long-legged bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher stretches to get a look at a heron-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To crane is to stretch out the neck, and a crane is also a tall long-legged waterbird.

clue.text: Can't meet Norway's revised law

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A law, once Norway amended it, can no longer be complied with.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is a statute that has been passed, so it is a law in the formal legislative sense.

clue.text: Heading to this perhaps, a little fast food and drink brought over in ship

indicators.note: the group goes inside the name of the ship

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth
a chip is a small piece of fast food

indicators.note: brought over means turned across, so the drink reads backwards

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: On board a vessel, grabbing some takeaway and a pint while sailing somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo is the ship of Jason and the Argonauts; the Greek islands of the Aegean were its home waters, so this group of islands is one place it might be heading.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a cluster of islands, a destination a ship like the Argo might well make for.

clue.text: On vacation coy man, after switch of heart, finds young bird

indicators.note: a switch of heart means the two central letters trade places
vacated means emptied, so the word loses its inside letters

parts.note: taken as written, then emptied to its outer letters
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A shy man on holiday changes his mind and spots a baby bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so it is a specific example of a young bird.

clue.text: Forces fierce females to embrace love

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Pressures formidable women into an embrace of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Forces is a verb here, as in coerces, not the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon is to coerce someone into doing something, so dragoons means forces in that verbal sense.

clue.text: Popular opening for initially overlooked creative person

indicators.note: overlooking the initial means its first letter is left out

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vent is an opening for air or gas
taken as written, then lose its first letter

explanation.surface: A popular opportunity for an artist who had been ignored at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor devises new things, so is by nature an original, creative person.

clue.text: New surgeon in hospital, foreign, one of pair to make rapid progress?

definitions.text: one of pair to make rapid progress?

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters are altered to an unfamiliar order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A new foreign surgeon at the hospital, one of a pair, is getting on fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Running shoes come in pairs and help an athlete move quickly, so one helps make rapid progress.

clue.text: At home sibling primarily tries to express convinced viewpoint

parts.note: in means at home
sis is short for sister

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: At home, a sister mainly tries to make her firmly held opinion known.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to state firmly and repeatedly what one believes, voicing a strongly held view.

clue.text: He advises some women to rest

indicators.note: some means a portion of the words that follow, a stretch of their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A man counsels some women to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted counsellor who guides a less experienced person, so one who advises.

clue.text: "No definite rules apply in these" — ex-Foreign Secretary at first argues referring to withdrawn appeal

definitions.text: No definite rules apply in these

parts.note: Sir Edward Grey, British Foreign Secretary at the outbreak of the First World War

indicators.note: at first points to the initial letter of the next word only

parts.note: the first letter of the word
re means concerning, referring to

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A former Foreign Secretary argues that there are no clear rules in some cases, citing an appeal that was withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words are the definition; the rest sounds like a legal argument but builds the letters. SA, sex appeal, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation with no clear-cut rules, where right and wrong are uncertain.

clue.text: Recycled traffic markers in Scottish location

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: traffic cones mark lanes on roads

explanation.surface: Old traffic cones being recycled somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Scone, near Perth, is where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of Scone.
explanation.definitionFit: Scone is a village and old royal site in Perthshire, so a place in Scotland.

clue.text: Prairie stove

definitions.meaning: first meaning: open grazing land in North America
second meaning: a large kitchen cooker

explanation.walkthrough: Prairie stove sounds like a cooker on a homestead; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The range is open grassland in the American West, and a range is also a large cooking stove.

clue.text: Get former pupil linked with Army elected

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
the TA, Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a politician who is elected is in

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil with military connections gets voted in.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or come by it, a direct synonym of get.

clue.text: One seeking influence to aim high — close to first

parts.note: to lob is to send a ball high in an arc
by means near
1st with the numeral 1 read as the Roman I

explanation.surface: An ambitious figure seeking power aims high and is nearly at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 1st written with the Roman numeral I for the digit is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobbyist works to persuade legislators on behalf of an interest group, so seeks political sway.

clue.text: After peace line of soldiers became smaller

indicators.note: after means the soldiers come behind, so the call for quiet goes first

parts.note: sh is a call for peace and quiet
a rank is a line of soldiers side by side

explanation.surface: Once the war ended, the army's ranks were reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Peace suggests the end of war, but it means quiet, the interjection for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrank is the past tense of shrink, to grow smaller, so the two phrases match.

clue.text: "Choosy" type the French (or Spanish) accommodated in particular area

indicators.note: being accommodated means being given room inside, so the article sits within the area

parts.note: a sector is a part or zone
le is French for the; el, the Spanish, also fits one place further along

explanation.surface: A fussy person is given lodging in a French or Spanish district.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket offers a choice: the Spanish article works just as well as the French one, since either sits in the area to give the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks players for a team, and the quotation marks admit choosy is meant literally as one who chooses.
